plan: Candidate006 abandons the whole-norm custom Function of candidate005 (which failed 8/1475 in formal training, hypothesized to be a BF16 accumulation/graph-association change) and instead ports candidate003's EXACT graph into a native C++/CUDA extension to remove Python-autograd and Triton launch-dispatch overhead. The normalization branch stays native ATen autograd exactly as candidate003: in C++ rms_norm, v=at::pow(x,2).mean({-1},true); v.add_(1.0013580322265625e-05) in-place (BF16 eps literal); r=at::rsqrt(v) — all BF16, autograd tracked. Only the final two multiplications are wrapped in ONE custom node FusedAffine (torch::autograd::Function) with separate input edges x, r, w, so r's gradient still flows back through the native pow/mean/rsqrt branch and accumulates with the direct-x gradient, mirroring candidate003's residual association. Forward (CUDA): y=BF16(BF16(x*r)*w) with the first product t=BF16(x*r) materialized and saved; save contiguous x,r,w,t. Backward (CUDA pointwise, no reductions): gw=BF16(g*w); dx_direct=BF16(gw*r); dr_terms=BF16(gw*x); dw_terms=BF16(g*t); then NATIVE at::Tensor sum_to_size reduces dr_terms to r.sizes() and dw_terms to w.sizes() — reduction order unchanged, norm gradient branches not combined. Returns {dx_direct, dr, dw} in input order x,r,w. All elementwise rounding uses the host/device c10::BFloat16 constructor (float->bf16 round) and static_cast<float> read-back after each product, so no cuda_bf16.h is required (CUDA 10.2 / CoreX 4.2 compatibility). Kernels use the current PyTorch CUDA stream on the input device under c10::cuda::CUDAGuard, 256 threads/block, and C10_CUDA_KERNEL_LAUNCH_CHECK. Outputs are at::empty_like (shape/dtype preserved). The Python candidate ONLY imports torch and the already-built module kda_bf16_affine_stage27_006, applies the same guard (nonempty BF16 CUDA, same device, hidden=512, 1D weight=512, eps exactly 1e-5; else NotImplementedError for native fallback), and calls the extension — it compiles/writes nothing, uses no cache/timer/env/network/system calls. This is portable pointwise fusion with no NVIDIA-specific hardware equivalence and no instruction-level claims. No speed or correctness is asserted ahead of the mandatory independent build plus full forward/dx/dw gates and the formal 1475-point training audit.
risks: ABI/compiler vendor compatibility: the extension must build and link against vendor Torch 2.4.1 / CoreX 4.2 CUDA with the available g++/nvcc under CUDA 10.2; a mismatch in c10::BFloat16 host/device constructor availability or ATen symbol ABI would fail the controller build or crash at import.

Staged BF16 rounding via c10::BFloat16(float) must match vendor-native BF16 rounding for each product exactly; if the extension's round-to-nearest differs from the native elementwise kernels in any tie case, dx/dw could diverge even though candidate003's Triton path passed.

Although the graph mirrors candidate003 (native norm branch + single affine node with separate x/r/w edges), the formal 1475-point training audit with FP32 gradient accumulation, master weights, and BF16 params across 3 steps remains mandatory; engine scheduling or accumulation-association differences could still surface as they did for candidate005.

sum_to_size is performed on the extension's BF16 term buffers via native ATen to keep reduction order identical to candidate003; any shape where broadcasting of r.sizes()/w.sizes() is ambiguous could mis-reduce, though the guards fix hidden=512/weight=512.
The kernels assume contiguous row-major layout (enforced by .contiguous() in forward and on the incoming grad); non-contiguous inputs are copied, adding traffic but not changing values/gradients.

No speed improvement is claimed; removing Python/Triton dispatch may still not beat native on the small [256,512] workload, and promotion depends solely on the independent build, exactness gates, and formal training comparator.
